timing.summary: Re-measured the paper2-fast-multiband speedup claims on this M5, single-threaded (OMP/OPENBLAS/VECLIB=1), median of 3 reps, warmup discarded, on a K=4 griz / N=15-per-band / well-conditioned (dy~0.02-0.05) synthetic dataset with an integer-f_min regular grid. All three package phase-maximizer paths agree to <4e-16. Deep-dip deferrals = 0 in every package-batched run, so the batched timings are pure batched compute. Findings: (1) The batched-vs-per-frequency-scan ratio is GRID-SIZE DEPENDENT and only partly reproduces the '12-14x @H8' claim. At the requested nfreq=2000 it is 9.71x (vs scan) / 8.72x (vs eigvals); at nfreq=8000 (the branch's bench/FINDINGS grid) it rises to 15.5x / 13.5x, landing in/above the 12-14x band. Cause: the batched path has a fixed NFFT/setup cost that amortizes over the grid (batched per-freq cost 127->81 us/freq as nfreq 2000->8000), while per-freq scan is ~constant at ~1240 us/freq. So the claim holds at the large grids used for the real PS1 search but is optimistic at small grids. H=4 gives 29.7x at nfreq=2000 (claim 'up to 36x'). (2) The '~38x/core A100' rests on a proto-CPU baseline (FINDINGS 97.7 us/LC/freq at B=256) that is NOT the best available single-thread CPU path. The proto is fastest at B=1 (77.9 us/LC/freq at H=8) and gets SLOWER per-LC as batch grows (B1/B64/B256 = 77.9/100.5/115.4 us/LC/freq; memory-bound at large B) - the opposite of the GPU, which needs B>=128 to saturate. The package's own batched path (127 us/freq single LC at nfreq=2000, 81 us/freq at nfreq=8000) is comparable-to-slower than proto B=1. Best single-thread CPU floor at H=8 is ~78-81 us/LC/freq. Against that floor the GPU (2.6 us/LC/freq, from FINDINGS - NOT re-measured here) is ~30x/core, not 38x; the 38x uses a CPU baseline penalized by the very large batch the GPU requires. My proto B=256 reproduction is 115-117 us/LC/freq (nfreq 2000 and 4000), ~18% above the claimed 97.7 (machine/config variance). (3) The 'per-freq cost ~H^1.3' claim is a rough, path-dependent middle estimate: 2-point (H4->H8) exponents are eigvals 1.09, proto-B1 1.58, proto-B256 1.77, batched 2.13; the per-freq-scan value (0.51) is meaningless (diluted by per-frequency param-object construction). The production batched path actually scales ~H^2.1 at fixed grid, so H8->H4 saves ~4.4x per-freq (more than the H^1.3 -> 2.46x the claim implies).
caveats: Single Apple M5 P-core equivalent, single-threaded (OMP_NUM_THREADS=OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1). No GPU measured here: the A100 2.6 us/LC/freq is taken from the branch FINDINGS.md, not re-verified; all GPU-multiple recomputations reuse that unverified 2.6 us figure.

The per-freq-scan denominator (multiband_template_periodogram, method='scan') builds a MultibandModelFitParams object per frequency; the batched path skips params. This Python overhead INFLATES the ratio in batched's favor, yet the ratio is still only 9.71x at nfreq=2000 - the true algorithmic speedup is <= the reported ratio. No powers-only per-frequency scan path exists in the public API, so this overhead cannot be excluded from the denominator without editing the package.

The batched-vs-per-freq ratio is grid-size dependent (fixed NFFT/setup amortization): 9.71x at nfreq=2000, 15.5x at nfreq=8000. Reporting a single 12-14x number is only valid at large nfreq (~4000-8000+, which is the PS1 regime); at nfreq=2000 it is 9.7x.

The proto CPU rate rises with batch B (memory-bound at large B): 77.9 (B=1) / 100.5 (B=64) / 115.4 (B=256) us/LC/freq at H=8. The FINDINGS '97.7' corresponds to B=256; my B=256 reproduction is 115-117 (nfreq 2000/4000), ~18% higher (machine/thermal/config variance). The exact FINDINGS config (B=256, nfreq=8000) was not run to completion (>8 min budget); cross-checked at nfreq=2000 and 4000, rate is ~nfreq-independent.

dy value is timing-neutral (weights do not change the flop count), so the package (dy~0.02-0.05) vs proto (same well-conditioned construction) dy difference does not affect any timing. Zero deep-dip deferrals in all package-batched runs confirms clean batched compute with no per-freq fallback contamination.
H-scaling exponents are crude 2-point (H=4 vs H=8) estimates (exponent = log2(t_H8/t_H4)); a multi-H fit would refine them.

'Best CPU path' at H=8 (~78-81 us/LC/freq) is the proto at B=1 and the package batched at large nfreq; these converge. The single-thread-fastest CPU operating point (B=1) is NOT the batch that saturates the GPU, so the 30x vs 38x gap reflects that CPU and GPU optima occur at different batch sizes, not a coding error - the proto-vs-proto 38x is internally consistent as same-code CPU-vs-GPU.
Scratch harness at experiments/paper2_gpu/trackB/_audit/bench.py; no tracked files modified, no git state touched.

parity.summary:
Re-verified all three parity claims numerically on an Apple M5 (CPU/numpy, single-threaded, OMP/BLAS pinned to 1). Scripts and raw JSON under experiments/paper2_gpu/trackB/_audit/ (audit_parity.py, decompose_a.py).

PART (a) — prototype (gpu_ftp_proto, xp=numpy) vs package floating_offsets, K=4 griz H=8, 9131 freqs, both direct sums. Original validate_vs_package.py reproduced exactly: median |dP| = 5.55e-17 (claim 5.6e-17, CONFIRMED), max |dP| = 0.1272 (claim ~0.13, CONFIRMED), power-spectrum argmax MATCHES (both f=1.81818, peak powers equal to 1e-16). BUT the fraction of frequencies with |dP| > 1e-9 is 30.9% (2826/9131), NOT ~4%; and the FINDINGS.md causal attribution ('max confined to the ~4% deep-|MM|-dip frequencies') is REFUTED. The argmax of |dP| sits at a well-conditioned frequency (min/max |MM| = 0.366, far from the 0.15 exact-fallback zone). A clean decomposition proves the divergence is entirely the omitted K.18 positive-amplitude filter, not deep-|MM| dips: (1) the K.18-only effect alone reproduces max = 0.1272 at the identical frequency and 100% of the >1e-9 frequencies; (2) the prototype matches the full package scan run with positive_amplitude=False to 6.1e-16 EVERYWHERE (0% exceed 1e-9) — so the proto's omission of dip-candidate seeding and exact-root fallback causes zero measurable divergence on this data; (3) only 3.7% of the divergent freqs are deep dips. The ~4% deep-dip fraction is itself real (3.6% below cond 0.15, 0% below the 3e-3 defer threshold) but is not where the error lives.

PART (b) — fresh synthetic K=4 griz, N=15/band, H=8, nfreq=3000, regular grid. FastMultibandTemplatePeriodogram.power(fast=True) [batched scan] vs method='eigvals' [reference], MATCHED NFFT summations: max |dP| = 3.33e-16, median 1.7e-17 (claim ~6.7e-16, CONFIRMED — same machine-epsilon order, within 2x; exact value is RNG/grid dependent float64 round-off). Deferral rate = 0.0 (0/3000; min combined-|MM| conditioning 0.086, well above _BATCHED_DEFER_RTOL=3e-3), CONFIRMING the code-comment claim that deferral fires ~0% on realistic griz — the whole 3.3e-16 parity is pure batched-scan-vs-eigvals with no per-frequency fallback. Both package paths apply K.18 (positive_amplitude=True), which is why they agree to machine epsilon.

PART (c) — K.18 positive-amplitude filter effect on case (b), via core.scan_polish_from_coefs on the assembled band-combined coefs (positive_amplitude=True vs False): 915/3000 = 30.5% of frequencies differ by more than 1e-12, max abs diff 0.1116. This bounds the error the prototype's K.18 omission can cause, and it matches part (a) both in magnitude (0.1116 vs 0.127) and in fraction (30.5% vs 30.9%), confirming the omitted K.18 filter — not deep-|MM| dips — is the source of the ~0.13 divergence.

Net: the magnitude numbers in FINDINGS.md (median 5.6e-17, max ~0.13, argmax match) are all correct, and the package-internal batched-scan-vs-eigvals parity (part b, 3.3e-16, 0% deferral) is solid. But the FINDINGS attribution of the max divergence to the '~4% deep-|MM|-dip frequencies' is wrong: the prototype is at machine-epsilon parity with the package's positive_amplitude=False scan, and diverges by up to 0.13 at ~31% of frequencies solely because it omits the K.18 positive-amplitude filter the package applies. The peak (period detection) is unaffected, but any use of the full spectrum shape/distribution would see the ~31% inflated points.
caveats: FINDINGS.md attribution is REFUTED, not just imprecise: 'max |dP| confined to ~4% deep-|MM|-dip frequencies' is false. The real cause is the prototype's omission of the K.18 positive-amplitude filter (positive_amplitude=True in the package, effectively False in the proto's scan_powers). 100% of the |dP|>1e-9 frequencies are explained by K.18; proto vs package-pos=False matches to 6.1e-16 everywhere.

The fraction with |dP|>1e-9 is 30.9% (part a), an order of magnitude larger than the '~4%' figure implied by FINDINGS. The ~4% is the genuine deep-dip fraction (3.6% below cond 0.15) but is not where the divergence occurs.

Detection peak is unaffected: power-spectrum argmax matches and peak power agrees to 1e-16 (the true-peak solution has non-negative amplitude, so K.18 does not change it). The divergence is at off-peak frequencies where the unconstrained best-fit amplitude is negative — so the proto's spectrum is systematically inflated there. This matters for any full-spectrum statistic (e.g. false-alarm/bootstrap distributions), not for locating the top peak.

Part (b)'s 6.7e-16 claim is only reproducible with MATCHED summations (batched fast=True vs eigvals fast=True, both NFFT) -> measured 3.33e-16. Comparing batched(fast=True, NFFT) against eigvals(fast=False, direct) gives 5.5e-9, which is the NFFT-vs-direct summation approximation, not the phase-maximizer; that larger number is not a maximizer parity failure.

Zero deferrals fired in part (b) (min conditioning 0.086 >> 3e-3), and zero deep-dip exact fallbacks were load-bearing in part (a), so these tests exercise well-conditioned griz only. They say nothing about the deep-dip/deferral machinery on adversarial phase-clumped data — the proto's simplified scan (no dip seeds, no exact fallback, no Aberth rooter) is untested here against genuinely deep dips.

All runs single-source (B=1 for the proto in part a) or per-frequency; single fixed RNG seeds (0 for a, 12345 for b). Machine-epsilon magnitudes (3e-16 vs claimed 6.7e-16) are seed/grid dependent and should be read as order-of-magnitude confirmations, not exact reproductions.
Scratch scripts written to experiments/paper2_gpu/trackB/_audit/ (audit_parity.py, decompose_a.py) per instructions; no tracked files modified, no git state touched.

rooter.summary: RE-VERIFIED: all three headline Aberth-rooter claims in experiments/paper2_gpu/rootfind/README.md hold on real FTP stationarity polynomials. NOTE the shipped rootfind/data/ npz fixtures are ABSENT, so retime.py/hybrid.py cannot run as-is; I rebuilt genuine degree-(6H-2) FTP stationarity polys in-memory through the real ftperiodogram pipeline (direct_summations_batched -> core.batched_YM_MM_from_sums -> core.batched_stationarity_coefs) and drove rootfinders.py exactly as retime.py/hybrid.py do. (1) SPEED ~3.2x at H8/D46: measured 3.1-3.3x in the hybrid block (batched_roots vs numpy_roots_loop) and 3.5x in the D-scaling isolate; grows with degree (2.5x@D22 -> 2.9x@D34 -> 3.5x@D46); batched companion-eigvals is ~1x (0.9-1.1x) as claimed. (2) ACCURACY ~2e-15: selected-power relative error vs numpy_roots_loop through the identical select_power path is pw_relmax 1.5-1.7e-15 at H=8 (median ~3e-16), at/below the claim. (3) 100% CONVERGENCE, 0 FALLBACKS on real FTP: 0 non-converged and 0 eigvals fallbacks across all 7 cases (H4/H6/H8 x N12/30/60), INCLUDING the rank-deficient H8_N12 case (N=12 < 2H+1=17); Aberth median 12-15 iters, max 18-21 (<60 cap). Hybrid safety-net verified on adversarial D46 inputs: clustered/multiple-root polys are exact-as-numpy (0.0 via 100% fallback), unit-circle case 5.6e-12 (aberth-accepted rows within tol=1e-12) -- graceful degradation confirmed. Machine: Apple M5, single-threaded, numpy 2.0.2, OMP/OPENBLAS/VECLIB=1. Driver scripts under experiments/paper2_gpu/trackB/_audit/.
caveats: Shipped rootfind/data/*.npz fixtures do NOT exist in the repo, so the original retime.py/hybrid.py cannot be run unmodified. I reconstructed equivalent REAL FTP stationarity polynomials in-memory via the actual ftperiodogram batched pipeline. Polynomials are genuine degree 6H-2 (D=46 at H=8), but the underlying synthetic dataset (RRL-like decaying-harmonic template, N points over a 90-day baseline, freqs 0.2-3.5) differs from whatever generated the original npz files; absolute speedups could shift a few tenths on other data, though ratios were stable across cases.

Timings reported are from nf=500 (hybrid block: H8 3.1-3.3x) and the nf=500 D-scaling isolate (D46 3.5x). A production-scale nf=20000 confirmation run was still executing (block-buffered, not yet flushed) when I finalized; timing RATIOS for this workload are essentially nf-independent and the nf=500 numbers already reproduce the ~3.2x claim, but the nf=20000 rerun was not captured in this report.
Durand-Kerner 'is ~8x slower and unreliable' was NOT independently re-benchmarked (not one of the three headline claims; the code path exists but I did not time it).

The 'inflate=1.2 halves iteration count (median 28->16 at D=46)' tuning claim was not A/B tested against inflate=1.0; I only observed median 12-15 iters at D=46 with the default inflate=1.2, consistent with the claimed post-tuning low end.

Accuracy was measured as selected-POWER relative error (README says 'phase/power'); best_phi was not separately tabulated, but selection is driven by the same projected roots so phase agreement is implied by the power agreement.
batched_roots default tol=1e-12/max_iter=60 were used (as in hybrid.py); robustness/D-scaling used batched_aberth with max_iter=60 to match retime.py (aberth's own default is tol=1e-13/max_iter=80).

minors.title: Factors in the §3 chain are on orthogonal axes (no inter-factor double-count); arithmetic self-consistent but ranges are not true min–max propagation
minors.claim: Q1: ÷12–14 (vectorization-over-frequency at fixed H=8), ÷3–5 (reduce H + grid), ×1.2–1.4 (extra work at candidates) are independent axes, so there is no double-counting BETWEEN factors. The chain's stated intermediate ranges are lightly rounded rather than fully propagated.
minors.evidence: True propagation: $1000/14=$71 (not the stated $100 low) … $2000/12=$167 (≈$170). Then ÷3–5 → $14–56 (stated $25–55). Then ×1.2–1.4 → true $17–78; headline states $30–70 (top rounded DOWN from ~$78). Low ends are rounded UP (conservative/costlier); final top rounded down (slightly optimistic). CAUTION: the TL;DR 'up to 36× at H=4' batching and the ÷12–14×÷3–5 chain are two decompositions of the SAME batched-H4 endpoint and DO agree (both give ≈÷40–47 from per-freq-H8: 36×1.1–1.3 ≈ 12–14×3.39), but combining them (e.g. ÷13 × ÷5 × 36) would double count — keep them separate.

minors.title: Context: PAPER2_BRIEF $300 cash ceiling assumed free Princeton P100s, which memory says are now gone — the nfreq/vocab undercounts land directly on cash
minors.claim: The compute envelope that bounds this program (PAPER2_BRIEF §9) is stale and optimistic in two ways that compound the cost findings above: it anchors to AUDIT §6 GPU numbers (memory: 'supersedes audit §6 GPU numbers ~10× too high') and assumes 2× Tesla P100 at $0 for the bulk (memory 2026-07-17: 'P100 GONE → all cloud/self-funded').

With P100s gone, there is no free-hardware fallback, so the corrected production ($150–350+ at 5× nfreq, more with K_vocab) and injection ($1500–3500+) costs collide with / blow through the $300 cash ceiling. This makes the nfreq and vocab findings go/no-go-relevant, not just precision nits.

minors.title: Search bands cover the injected true frequency range (no true-signal deflation), but alias crediting is asymmetric at the Bailey-box edges and harmonic-crediting can inflate RRc
minors.claim: SEARCH_BAND RRab (0.9,3.4) c/d covers the injected true range [1.111,2.273] and RRc (1.8,6.5) covers [2.222,5.000] -- both with margin, so no injected truth is out of band and there is NO silent deflation of the true recovery rate. However the aliases that classify_recovery credits are only partially reachable: at the short-period edge P/2 (2*f_true) falls above the band (RRab 4.55>3.4; RRc 10>6.5) and at the long-period edge 2P (f/2) falls below (RRab 0.56<0.9; RRc 1.11<1.8), and several day-beats leave the band at the edges. Net effect is on the alias BREAKDOWN, not the headline rate, and it is symmetric across H so it does not bias the paired comparison. Separately, for near-sinusoidal RRc the in-band P/2 (2f) harmonic IS reachable and count_harmonics=True credits it as 'recovered', which optimistically counts a period-halved lock as success for a search that actually needs the true period.
minors.evidence: Analytic check (_audit): RRab band covers [1.111,2.273]=True; RRc covers [2.222,5.000]=True. Edge aliases: f_true=2.273 -> P/2=4.55 out; f_true=1.111 -> 2P=0.56 out; RRc f_true=5.0 -> P/2=10 out, f_true=2.222 -> 2P=1.11 out. recovery.harmonic_alias_set includes 0.5,2,1/3,3 + day_beats(1,2)+year_beats(1); classify_recovery(count_harmonics=True) credits any match.

minors.title: Frequency grid df=1/(oversample*H*T) is adequate and, because df scales as 1/H matching the peak width, introduces no differential bias between H values
minors.claim: converged_grid is sound for both requirements. (i) Peak-finding: since the H-harmonic peak half-width ~1/(H*T) and df=1/(os*H*T), samples-per-peak = os is CONSTANT across H, so lower H is not grid-starved relative to high H and the paired H-loss is not a grid artifact -- the elegant part of the design. (ii) Recovery tolerances: at f~2 c/d the argmax quantization df/2 is ~1.6e-5/f fractional (H=8) to ~1.3e-4 (H=1), far inside rtol=0.01; for phase_coherence the requirement |df|*T<0.5 => |df|<3.85e-4 c/d at T=1300, and even the coarsest grid (H=1, os=3) has df=2.56e-4 with quantization 1.3e-4 < 3.85e-4. So argmax-on-grid is fine. Minor caveat only: os=3 gives ~3 samples across the FWHM at H=1 (bare, though standard for argmax), and the f_lo snap-down is correct for the NFFT integer-multiple constraint. Not a source of curve error.
minors.evidence: df=1/(os*H*T): H=8,os=3,T1300 -> 3.2e-5 c/d (nfreq~77k over RRab band, matches profiled 76792); H=1 -> 2.56e-4. rtol=0.01 and delta_phi_max=0.5 tolerances computed above. converged_grid snaps f_start=floor(f_lo/df)*df, n=ceil((f_hi-f_start)/df)+1 covers f_hi.

minors.title: Paired-loss SE is the correct first-order McNemar SE, but the disagree=0 -> SE=0 case (which the saturated defaults produce) reports a misleadingly certain zero loss
minors.claim: summarize() uses se=sqrt(disagree)/n where disagree=b01+b10 is the discordant-pair count. This equals the standard McNemar SE for the paired proportion difference (b01-b10)/n to first order (it drops only the small -(b01-b10)^2/n^3 correction, making it slightly conservative) -- so the formula is essentially right, good catch that it is paired not naive. The defect is the disagree==0 branch setting se=0.0: in the saturated regime the defaults create (H2 and H8 both recover everything), disagree=0 and the report reads 'rate loss = +0.000 +/- 0.000', implying a certain zero when the correct statement is an upper bound (rule of three: with 0/ n discordant, ~3/n, e.g. ~1.2% at n=256). This directly reinforces the false 'low-H is safe' conclusion.
minors.evidence: b1 lines ~118-126: a,b bool arrays; loss=mean(b)-mean(a); disagree=sum(a!=b); se=sqrt(disagree)/n if disagree else 0.0. Empirical: default and realistic-noise RRab runs gave disagree=0/10 -> se would print 0.000.

minors.title: Per-source cadence seed is silently ignored: the cadence realization is drawn from the injection RNG, not the ps1_cadence seed
minors.claim: inject() builds rng=RandomState(seed) and passes random_state=rng into simulate_multiband_lightcurve, which calls cadence.sample(rng); SyntheticCadence.sample uses the PASSED rng whenever it is not None, so self.random_state (the seed set by ps1_cadence, = seed*100003+i in build_population) is never used to draw epochs. Consequences: (1) the documented independent cadence seeding is dead code -- changing the cadence seed alone does nothing; (2) epochs, period, tau, band offsets and noise are all drawn from ONE shared RNG stream per source rather than independent streams, so cadence and signal parameters are correlated draws. It still yields a distinct valid realization per source (inject seed varies with i), so it does not by itself corrupt the population, but it is a latent surprise that will bite anyone who tries to hold the cadence fixed while reseeding noise, or vice versa.
minors.evidence: lib.inject: rng=np.random.RandomState(seed); simulate_multiband_lightcurve(...,random_state=rng); simulate does rng=_as_rng(random_state) then cadence.sample(rng). SyntheticCadence.sample: rng=_as_rng(self.random_state if rng is None else rng) -> passed rng wins. build_population passes seed*100003+i to ps1_cadence (unused) and seed*7919+i to inject (the effective seed).

minors.title: Throughput timing is mildly optimistic: min-of-reps captures peak boost clock, and H2D/D2H transfers are excluded from the timed region
minors.claim: bench_throughput.py takes tb=min(ts) over reps=3 (line 69). Combined with the acknowledged idle-210MHz->boost behavior, min-of-3 systematically selects the highest-clock run, so 48 LC/s is a peak-clock rate; the 58-GPU-hr / '2.4 days' extrapolation (FINDINGS) assumes that peak is sustained over a multi-day run. Separately, inputs are staged onto the device inside make_batch via xp.asarray before timing, and the result is never .get()'d (only Stream.synchronize, line 63), so neither H2D of light-curve data nor D2H of the (B,nfreq) powers is in the timed region. The numpy baseline also runs with no OMP/OPENBLAS/VECLIB thread cap set, so the 'one M5 P-core' claim is unenforced (this cuts conservatively -- multithreading would make the CPU look faster).
minors.evidence: bench_throughput.py: line 65 warmup run(); lines 67-69 timing loop with min(); line 63 sync-only, no device->host copy; make_batch (lines 40-43) wraps arrays in xp.asarray so cupy inputs pre-exist on device. Transfers are small relative to compute (LC arrays are B*N*K floats; powers B*nfreq) so the transfer omission is minor, but the peak-clock selection means the sustained cost estimate is a floor on time / ceiling on throughput.

minors.title: The 8 GB phi-powers argument does not rule out cupy-level fusion; it is a large-chunk artifact
minors.claim: FINDINGS.md argues the precomputed-phi-powers variant is intrinsically memory-bound because the (nB,Cmax,ncoef) tensor is ~8 GB/chunk, concluding 'Neither cupy-level form is the answer'. The 8 GB is specific to a large chunk; the tensor scales linearly with chunk, so a smaller chunk keeps it O(1 GB) and the memory objection evaporates. The reasoning over-generalizes from one configuration.
minors.evidence: _audit arithmetic: MM phi-powers tensor = nB*Cmax*(4H+1)*16 bytes with nB=B*chunk, Cmax=4H. At B=256,chunk=2048 (the proto's default chunk in floating_offsets_powers) = 8.25 GiB (matches '~8GB'); at chunk=256 = 1.03 GiB (fits easily). So a smaller-chunk phi-powers or partially-fused cupy variant is not excluded by memory -- whether it is faster is simply untested here (no GPU). The custom-CUDA-fusion recommendation stands, but the specific 8GB rebuttal of cupy fusion is not airtight.

minors.title: direct_sums product-to-sum assembly verified bit-exact vs the package, including the 2H-th harmonic (no off-by-one)
minors.claim: gpu_ftp_proto.direct_sums (Sn/Cn with ak=|k-j|, S[...,ak-1] and diagonal overwrite; Sp/Cp=S/C[...,j+k+1]) is mathematically identical to ftperiodogram.summations._direct_stacked_sums_chunk / direct_summations_batched, differing only by the added batch axis. The j+k+1 index reaches 2H-1 at j=k=H-1, which is the 2H-th harmonic, and C/S are computed for harmonics 1..2H, so the top harmonic is present with no off-by-one.

The FTP peak half-width ~1/(H*T), so lowering H widens the peak; dividing df by H holds samples-per-peak-width (oversample) CONSTANT across H. 2) "This bites the faint completeness edge" is refuted by measurement. Independent reproduction with the project's own b1 design (BV-2025 real RRab template shapes, synthetic PS1-like griz cadence, floating_offsets, K=4 detection vocab, per-H converged matched grids), single-threaded (OMP=1):

verified.title: Synthetic PS1 cadence draws uniform-in-season epochs with no same-night pairing or night clustering, so it lacks the daily-alias window structure that dominates real PS1 3pi recovery and dip rates

This structurally biases exactly the aliasing-driven quantities B1/B4 are meant to measure, and it is not fixed by the ZTF stressor since ZTF (g/r, different window) is not PS1.

Every substantive assertion — 31% of frequencies, up to 0.127, median hides it (dominated by the 69% machine-epsilon matches), argmax/peak unaffected because the true signal has positive amplitude, cause is K.18/positive_amplitude, one-directional background inflation, FINDINGS.md mislabels it — is independently reproduced.
